To use AT&T Video Call, all parties must have Video Call-capable devices, located in HD Voice coverage, with a rate plan eligible to use Video Call.
Each Video Call uses both voice and data. The voice portion of the call counts as voice minutes, and the video portion counts as data under your wireless rate plan.

Once you have started a Video Call, it will seamlessly switch to Wi-Fi if your device has access to the Internet through its Wi-Fi connection. To continue a video call on Wi-Fi, you must also remain connected to the AT&T wireless network. No voice or data charges apply to Video Call over Wi-Fi.

The Video Call icon tells you when you\'re able to make a video call. Other AT&T subscribers can see if you\'re capable of receiving video calls. This capability indication may not function with subscribers on other carriers.
You can disable AT&T Video Call in Call Settings on your device.
